title: Maximum Score After Applying Operations on a Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a set of edges connecting these nodes, along with an array of node values, you can increase your score by selecting any node, adding its value to your score, and setting its value to zero.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a set of edges connecting these nodes, along with an array of node values, you can increase your score by selecting any node, adding its value to your score, and setting its value to zero. The tree must remain healthy, meaning the sum of values on the path from the root to any leaf node must not be zero. Determine the maximum score you can achieve while ensuring the tree remains healthy.
constraints: Collecting a node adds its value to the score and sets that node value to zero.
After operations, every root-to-leaf path must retain at least one nonzero node; maximize score.
hints: Maximizing collected score equals minimizing value that must remain to protect every root-leaf path.
At a leaf its value must remain; internally retain either this node or enough protection in every child subtree.
Return min(node value, sum child retained costs), then subtract root cost from total.
Those are the only two ways every descendant leaf path can retain a nonzero node.
editorial: Those are the only two ways every descendant leaf path can retain a nonzero node.
